context: Reading a suite for the specific ways parallel workers collide. Five files each carry one hazard - a process-wide environment write, a fixed listening port, a fixed absolute file path, a test-name-derived database key, and a fixed sleep standing in for synchronisation - and money.test.js is genuinely safe. Predicted baseline failure: the agent finds the port and the temp path, which look like collisions, and misses the environment write and the test-name seed, which look like ordinary test code. The sleep is usually reported as slowness rather than as a correctness hazard that gets worse under contention. A further common error is flagging the safe file to be thorough.

checklist.name: Environment write identified
checklist.description: config.test.js is flagged because process.env is per-process and shared by every test in that worker, so one test's write or delete decides another's read. Omitting this scores zero - it is the least visible of the five and the one most likely to be dismissed as normal test code.

checklist.name: Fixed port identified
checklist.description: server.test.js is flagged because port 3000 is bound exclusively: the first worker binds and the rest fail to listen.

checklist.name: Fixed file path identified
checklist.description: logging.test.js is flagged because /tmp/test.log is a single path every worker truncates and appends to, so assertions read another worker's writes.

checklist.name: Test-name-derived key identified
checklist.description: db.test.js is flagged because deriving the seed key from the test name is only unique while names are unique - two files with a similarly named test collide in the shared database, and the collision is invisible in the source of either. Omitting this scores zero.

checklist.name: Fixed sleep identified as a correctness hazard
checklist.description: queue.test.js is flagged because a fixed wait substitutes for a completion signal, and contention on shared workers makes the wait insufficient rather than merely slow. Reporting it only as a performance cost scores at most half.

checklist.name: Safe file reported as safe
checklist.description: MUST NOT flag money.test.js. It touches no shared surface and is explicitly listed among the files needing no work. Reporting it as unsafe scores zero on this criterion: a report that flags everything gives the team no way to prioritise.

checklist.name: Fix given per finding
checklist.description: Each flagged file carries a concrete remedy - per-test environment save and restore or injected configuration, an ephemeral port, a per-worker temporary directory, a unique generated key, and an event-based wait. A report that describes hazards without remedies scores zero here.

checklist.name: Sequencing given
checklist.description: The report states an order of work and says which fixes are independent, rather than presenting five items as an unordered list.
